summary: Valley County lookout first used in 1921, with a 1977 R-6 flat cab; standing, with the concrete base dated 1950 or 1956 and current staffing unconfirmed.

access.note: Listed as hike-in by Idaho Fire Lookouts. No closure or rental notice was found in the pages read. Current staffing is unconfirmed; the association's undated page does not name Tripod.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in per Idaho Fire Lookouts; no route description was read.

events.note: First lookout: a California Region 5 Plan 4A cabin on a six-foot open timber tower (NHLR). Firelookout.com describes a six-foot wooden tower topped by a live-in cab.
R1/L-4 cabin replaced the first cab. Idaho Fire Lookouts dates the L-4 cab to 1934; firelookout.com says the L-4 tower came in the 1930s.
Concrete base added (NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts). Firelookout.com dates the concrete base to 1956.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, October 3, 2020.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts date the concrete base to 1950; firelookout.com dates it to 1956. The story gives both.

The NHLR and firelookout.com say the Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association staffs the lookout. The association's undated employment page names two other lookouts and not Tripod. The story reports the disagreement and does not claim a current season.
The NHLR gives 8,082 ft (2,463 m); firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 8086 ft. The story uses the NHLR figure.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 1.8 has no source among the pages read, so it is omitted. Concrete base 1950 (NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus 1956 (firelookout.com). Elevation 8,082 ft (NHLR) versus 8086 ft (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts). The association's name is spelled Protection on the NHLR and Protective elsewhere; the story uses Protective. Current staffing is unconfirmed: the association's undated employment page names only Brundage and Lookout mountains. No closure or rental notice was found. The brief's events for 1921, 1977 and 2020 are supported.
